symbols.name: last-axis variable
symbols.meaning: The variable of the last cyclic axis, with x_d^r = 1.
symbols.quote: Cyclic convolution along the last axis is multiplication in $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$, where $x_d$ is the variable of that axis and $x_d^r=1$.

symbols.name: twist phase
symbols.meaning: The number e^{\pi i/r}, a primitive 2r-th root of unity with \zeta^r = -1.
symbols.quote: Let $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, a primitive $2r$-th root of unity, so $\zeta^r=-1$.

symbols.name: twist map
symbols.meaning: The ring isomorphism from C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1) to the negacyclic ring sending x_d to \zeta y.
symbols.quote: Define the ring map $\Theta$ from $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$ to $\mathcal R_r$ by $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$.

symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of axes of the array f.
symbols.quote: Let a complex array $f$ have $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

symbols.name: total entries
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the array f in all.
symbols.quote: Let a complex array $f$ have $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

symbols.name: number of records
symbols.meaning: The number of lines along the last axis, T/r.
symbols.quote: Then $M=T/r$ is the number of lines along the last axis.

symbols.name: record identification
symbols.meaning: Reads each line along the last axis as a polynomial in the negacyclic ring.
symbols.quote: The map $\iota$ reads each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$.

symbols.name: diagonal twist
symbols.meaning: Multiplies entry k of each line by \zeta^{\pm k}.
symbols.quote: Let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

symbols.name: ring convolution
symbols.meaning: The ring convolution that convolves the first d-1 axes over the negacyclic ring and includes the division by T.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution of [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md): it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$ and includes the division by $T$.

symbols.name: normalized cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The composite D_-\iota^{-1}\mathcal M_r(\iota D_+ f,\iota D_+ g), equal to f*g/T.
symbols.quote: Call the composite $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$, the normalized complex cyclic convolution:

relations.predicate: converts the last cyclic axis into
relations.quote: The twist converts the last cyclic axis into the coordinate of the [Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1](ring-y.md), where $y^r=-1$ instead.
The twist reproduces [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) on that axis, because untwisting restores the wrap.

derivations.quote: Let $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, a primitive $2r$-th root of unity, so $\zeta^r=-1$. Define the ring map $\Theta$ from $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$ to $\mathcal R_r$ by $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$.

It is well defined because $(\zeta y)^r=(-1)(-1)=1$, so $x_d^r-1$ goes to zero.

Since $\Theta(x_d^k)=\zeta^k y^k$, $\Theta$ is diagonal on the bases $(x_d^k)$ and $(y^k)$, multiplying coefficient $k$ by $\zeta^k\ne0$. It is therefore an isomorphism, with inverse multiplying coefficient $k$ by $\zeta^{-k}$.
The coefficient of $y^j$ is thus $\zeta^j$ times the cyclic coefficient, and untwisting by $\zeta^{-j}$ restores it with the correct sign.
Then $\iota D_+$ applies $\Theta$ to every line, with inverse $D_-\iota^{-1}$.
